historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, Volume 13, Chapter: The Battle of Hunayn and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
historical_references.context: Qashid ibn Sa'd was the governor of Kufa during the early caliphate. He is known to have revolted against Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph, during the Battle of Siffin. The revolt was eventually suppressed, and Qashid was killed in the fighting.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's The History of al-Tabari: From the Beginning of the Islamic Era to the End of the Umayyad Caliphate, Volume 3, Chapter: The Battle of Hunayn.
historical_references.context: Qashid ibn Sa'd was a prominent Arab leader who joined the Muslim army during the Battle of Hunayn. He was given the title 'al-Qasri' (the resident of al-Qasr) due to his bravery and leadership skills. After the battle, he was appointed as the governor of the Yemen region by the caliph, Umar ibn al-Khattab.
